design_rationale: The paper explicitly describes a "multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, phase 2/3 study" in which "On day 1, patients were randomized in a double-blind manner to either placebo, dapagliflozin 5-mg, or dapagliflozin 10-mg daily," with randomization stratified by pre-enrollment antihyperglycemic therapy (NCT00663260).

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants were randomized in a stratified, double-blind fashion with a prespecified 84-per-arm target, and baseline demographic, glycemic and renal characteristics were well balanced across arms, consistent with chance; the sequence-generation/concealment mechanism is not described in detail but double-blind placebo-controlled design and balance make concealment likely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "On day 1, patients were randomized in a double-blind manner to either placebo, dapagliflozin 5-mg, or dapagliflozin 10-mg daily... Randomization was stratified based on pre-enrollment antihyperglycemic therapy"; "Groups generally appeared to be balanced with respect to key demographic and baseline characteristics (Table 1)."

domain_judgments.rationale: Blinding of patients and investigators was maintained with matching placebo, but co-intervention with protocol-permitted glycemic rescue and unrecorded sliding-scale insulin adjustments may have differed between arms and affected the glycemic endpoint, and the primary analysis excluded post-rescue data with LOCF rather than a strict intention-to-treat approach.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Unmeasured differential behavior with respect to sliding scale and other adjustments of insulin between placebo and dapagliflozin could blunt the apparent efficacy of dapagliflozin."

domain_judgments.rationale: Attrition was large and differential (24-week completion 73.8% placebo vs 86.7%/81.2% dapagliflozin; only 139/252 completed 104 weeks), outcome data at later timepoints were extremely sparse and imbalanced (HbA1c change at week 104 based on n=4 placebo vs 8 and 10 dapagliflozin), and missingness was handled chiefly by last-observation-carried-forward without sensitivity analyses demonstrating robustness to informative missingness.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The short-term completion rate was lower for placebo (73.8%) than for dapagliflozin 5-mg (86.7%) and 10-mg (81.2%) groups, the main difference being higher rate of discontinuations for adverse events for placebo"; "Change at week 104 | 4 | -0.67 [0.41] | 8 | -1.21 [0.38] | 10 | -0.75 [0.22]"

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary and secondary outcomes (HbA1c, FPG, weight, eGFR, creatinine clearance) are objective laboratory/physical measures assessed identically across arms by a central laboratory under double-blind conditions, minimizing assessor influence.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "A central laboratory evaluated the assays for the efficacy and safety outcomes, using high-performance liquid chromatography for HbA1c and colorimetric indicator for plasma creatinine and urinary albumin:creatinine ratio."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered with a clearly prespecified primary endpoint and analysis model, but the protocol/SAP is not available for checking, multiple analytic variants were reported (with/without post-rescue data, LOCF, completers, longitudinal repeated measures) and emphasized findings include explicitly post-hoc subgroup analyses by CKD stage, with the industry sponsor employing two authors.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Post-hoc analysis by baseline chronic kidney disease (CKD) stage (Table 4) showed a larger reduction in adjusted mean change in HbA1c and FPG... Several sensitivity analyses (completers, longitudinal repeated-measure analysis with or without data after rescue) were performed."

overall_summary: Although this registered, stratified, double-blind placebo-controlled trial had sound randomization and objective, centrally measured outcomes, it is at high overall risk of bias because of substantial and differential attrition (73.8% vs 86.7%/81.2% completion at 24 weeks; only 139/252 at 104 weeks, with week-104 HbA1c based on 4–10 patients per arm) handled mainly by LOCF. Additional concerns arise from potential differential insulin/rescue co-interventions and from reliance on post-hoc subgroup and multiple analytic approaches in an industry-sponsored, underpowered study.

design_rationale: Explicitly a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled parallel-group Phase 3 trial with 1:1 allocation stratified by pre-enrolment glucose-lowering therapy, using an IVRS/IWRS to assign randomization codes (NCT02413398).

domain_judgments.rationale: Central IVRS/IWRS allocation with stratification ensures concealment, and baseline characteristics were broadly balanced (minor imbalances in HbA1c distribution and age category are compatible with chance given n≈320).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Eligible patients were assigned a unique randomization code using an interactive voice response system (IVRS) or interactive web response system (IWRS)... Demographics and baseline characteristics were balanced between treatment groups"

domain_judgments.rationale: Double-blind with matching placebo and a single-blind placebo lead-in; rescue medication was pre-specified, balanced between arms (5.0% vs 6.2%), and the primary analysis used all randomized/treated patients with an MMRM censoring post-rescue data per protocol.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "randomized, double-blind, two-arm, parallel group, placebo-controlled... matching placebo"

domain_judgments.rationale: Completion was high and similar across arms (93.1% vs 90.7% completed double-blind treatment; 97.5% vs 95.7% completed the study), and MMRM under missing-at-random plus pre-specified sensitivity analyses support robustness.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "most also completed the 24-week double-blind treatment period (149 patients [93.1%] in the dapagliflozin group and 146 patients [90.7%] in the placebo group)"

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome (HbA1c) is an objective laboratory measure assessed identically at scheduled visits in both arms under double-blind conditions, so assessor knowledge could not plausibly bias it.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The primary efficacy outcome was mean change from baseline in HbA1c at Week 24."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered (NCT02413398) with a publicly available protocol, the primary and secondary endpoints and a pre-specified sequential testing procedure and analysis model are reported as planned; industry sponsorship/authorship is noted but does not by itself indicate selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "This study is registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT02413398). The study protocol is available online... A sequential testing procedure was employed to accommodate multiple comparisons"

overall_summary: A well-conducted, pre-registered, double-blind placebo-controlled Phase 3 trial with central randomization, balanced baseline characteristics, high and balanced retention, an objective laboratory primary outcome, and pre-specified analysis with multiplicity control; all five RoB 2 domains were judged low risk. Industry funding/authorship is a residual consideration but did not raise any domain above low risk.

design_rationale: The paper explicitly describes a phase 3, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial in which eligible patients "were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive bexagliflozin (20 mg) or placebo," with stratified randomization via a central interactive web response system (NCT02836873).

domain_judgments.rationale: Stratified 1:1 allocation was performed through a central interactive web response system with codes held by an uninvolved statistician (adequate concealment), and baseline characteristics including stratification variables were similar between arms.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Randomization and study drug allocation were performed through a central interactive web response system... Allocation codes were maintained by a designated statistician not involved in study operations." / "Baseline characteristics, including variables used to stratify randomization (Table 1)... were similar between treatment groups."

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants, investigators, and sponsor were blinded for the trial duration, rescue medication was permitted by protocol in both arms (more often in placebo), and effectiveness analyses were intention-to-treat with results also presented including post-rescue values.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Investigators, patients, and the sponsor team remained blinded to allocation groups for the duration of the trial." / "Effectiveness analyses were performed in an intention-to-treat manner."

domain_judgments.rationale: Nearly all randomized participants (312) contributed data, with per-visit counts showing minimal attrition (e.g., 149–152 of 155/157 at week 24) and similar early withdrawal rates between arms assessed by Kaplan-Meier; mixed-model repeated measures plus LOCF after rescue were used.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The effect of group assignment on early withdrawal was assessed using Kaplan-Meier analysis." / "early withdrawal rates (Fig S2) were similar between treatment groups."

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome (HbA1c) is an objective laboratory measure processed at regional central facilities identically across arms under double-blind conditions, with blinded adjudication of cardiovascular events.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Samples for laboratory testing were processed at regional central facilities." / "All suspected major adverse cardiac events (MACE) were forwarded to a cardiovascular end point committee for blinded adjudication."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered with a pre-specified protocol/statistical analysis plan, no interim analysis, and the pre-stated primary endpoint is reported; however, the protocol, SAP, and participant data are explicitly not available for verification, and the sponsor/academic group authored the analysis plan, leaving residual uncertainty about analysis choices (e.g., LOCF imputation after rescue as the primary approach).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Other supporting documents (study protocol, statistical analysis plan, informed consent form, clinical study report, and analytic code) will not be available."

overall_summary: This well-conducted, registered, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial had low risk in randomization, intervention adherence/analysis, missing data, and outcome measurement domains. Overall judgment of "some concerns" is driven solely by Domain 5, since the protocol, statistical analysis plan, and analytic code are explicitly unavailable, preventing verification that the reported primary analysis (including the LOCF-after-rescue approach) was pre-specified.

design_rationale: The CREDENCE trial explicitly describes double-blind 1:1 random allocation to canagliflozin or matching placebo using randomly permuted blocks with stratification by screening eGFR category: "The patients were randomly assigned in a double-blind fashion (1:1) to receive either canagliflozin (100 mg orally once daily) or matching placebo with the use of randomly permuted blocks."

domain_judgments.rationale: A stratified permuted-block random sequence was used with double-blind allocation (matching placebo, central/sponsor-managed multicentre trial with a placebo run-in), and baseline characteristics across 4401 patients were closely balanced (age, sex, eGFR 56.3 vs 56.0, HbA1c 8.3 vs 8.3, UACR 923 vs 931), consistent with chance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The patients were randomly assigned in a double-blind fashion (1:1) to receive either canagliflozin (100 mg orally once daily) or matching placebo with the use of randomly permuted blocks, with stratification according to the category of estimated GFR ... The baseline characteristics of the patients were similar in the two groups

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants, carers and investigators were blinded by a matching placebo, the primary analysis was intention-to-treat with a stratified Cox model, and although 27.3% discontinued study drug (adherence 84%) and a 2016 amputation-related protocol amendment permitted temporary treatment interruption, these deviations were balanced across groups and do not undermine the ITT estimate of the assignment effect.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In the intention-to-treat population, we used a stratified Cox proportional-hazards model to analyze the primary and secondary outcomes ... 1201 patients (27.3%) in the two groups had discontinued therapy ...; the rate of adherence to the trial regimen was 84% during follow-up.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome/vital status ascertainment was near-complete (99.1% alive with follow-up or died before final visit; vital status known for 4395/4401 = 99.9%; consent withdrawn by only 16 patients), and a sensitivity analysis imputing missing data gave nearly identical results (HR 0.69 vs 0.70).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 4361 patients (99.1%) were either alive with follow-up at the end of the trial or had died before the final follow-up visit ... vital status was ascertained for all but 6 patients (4395 [99.9%]) ... Nearly identical results were shown in sensitivity analyses that included imputation of missing data (hazard ratio, 0.69; 95% CI, 0.59 to 0.82)

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary composite comprised objective, hard endpoints (ESKD, doubling of creatinine confirmed by central laboratory, renal/cardiovascular death) measured identically in both groups and adjudicated by independent committees blinded to treatment assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All renal and cardiovascular outcomes that were part of the primary and secondary outcomes, as well as key safety outcomes ... were adjudicated by independent adjudication committees whose members were unaware of trial-group assignments.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered (NCT02065791) with a published design paper, a publicly available protocol, a prespecified primary outcome and a prespecified hierarchical secondary testing sequence with alpha-spending, which strongly limits selective reporting; however, the trial was stopped early at a planned interim analysis on an efficacy boundary, which the authors acknowledge may overestimate effect sizes, and subgroup/exploratory analyses were reported without adjustment for multiple testing.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: First, the trial was stopped early at a planned interim analysis, which may have limited the power for some secondary outcomes and may increase the risk of overestimating effect sizes. ... Subgroup analyses were assessed by tests for the interaction between the trial group and the subgroup ... without adjustment for multiple testing.

overall_summary: This large, pre-registered, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial has strong methodology across randomization, blinding, ITT analysis, near-complete follow-up (99.9% vital status) and blinded independent adjudication of objective endpoints (all low risk). The overall rating of "some concerns" is driven solely by Domain 5: early termination at a planned interim efficacy boundary (acknowledged by the authors as potentially overestimating effect size) plus unadjusted subgroup/exploratory reporting.

design_rationale: The DAPA-CKD trial explicitly randomly assigned 4304 participants to dapagliflozin 10 mg or matching placebo using a sequestered fixed-randomization schedule with balanced blocks and an interactive voice/Web-response system: "Our trial was a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter clinical trial."

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation used a sequestered, block-balanced, stratified randomization schedule administered via a central interactive voice/Web-response system (concealing allocation), and baseline characteristics in Table 1 were closely balanced across the two 2152-participant groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Participants were randomly assigned to receive dapagliflozin (10 mg once daily) or matching placebo, in accordance with the sequestered, fixed-randomization schedule, with the use of balanced blocks to ensure an approximate 1:1 ratio of the two regimens... Investigators used an interactive voice-response or Web-response system to determine trial-group assignments."

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and all trial personnel were blinded with identically packaged tablets, discontinuation rates were similar between groups (12.7% vs 14.4%), and the primary efficacy analysis followed intention-to-treat including all randomized participants.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Participants and all trial personnel (except the members of the independent data monitoring committee) were unaware of the trial-group assignments. Dapagliflozin and placebo were packaged identically, with uniform tablet appearance, labeling, and administration schedules... The primary efficacy analysis was based on the intention-to-treat population, which included all the participants who had undergone randomization."

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were essentially complete: 99.7% of participants completed the trial, only 11 (0.3%) withdrew consent, and vital status was unknown for just 5 participants (0.1%), far too few to bias the effect estimates.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "In all, 4289 participants (99.7%) completed the trial (i.e., were alive with follow-up data available at the trial completion visit or had died during follow-up). A total of 11 participants (0.3%) withdrew consent, and vital status was ascertained for all but 5 participants (0.1%)."

domain_judgments.rationale: The composite outcome comprised objective, clinically meaningful events ascertained identically in both groups via central laboratory creatinine measurements and adjudicated by an independent committee blinded to trial-group assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "An independent committee whose members were unaware of the trial-group assignments adjudicated all primary and secondary outcomes, except for a sustained decline in the estimated GFR of at least 50% and a sustained estimated GFR of less than 15 ml per minute per 1.73 m2, which were ascertained from central laboratory measurements."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered (NCT03036150) with a published protocol, prespecified statistical analysis plan and hierarchical closed testing, but the prespecified formal interim analysis was removed from the protocol during the trial and the trial was then stopped early for efficacy on a data monitoring committee recommendation without an apparent prespecified stopping boundary, which introduces some concern about the timing/selection of the reported analysis (and possible overestimation of effect).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "In brief, a formal interim analysis was originally planned when 75% of primary outcome events had occurred. However, during the conduct of the trial it became apparent that the interim analysis would occur close to the end of the trial. The executive committee therefore decided to remove the interim analysis from the protocol."

overall_summary: This large, well-conducted, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial had concealed block randomization with balanced baseline characteristics, near-complete follow-up (99.7%), blinded independent outcome adjudication, and intention-to-treat analysis, all rated low risk. The overall judgment of "some concerns" is driven solely by Domain 5: the prespecified interim analysis was removed from the protocol mid-trial and the trial was subsequently stopped early for efficacy, which raises concern about the selection/timing of the reported result and potential overestimation of the treatment effect.

design_rationale: EMPA-KIDNEY is explicitly described as an "international, randomized, parallel-group, double-blind, placebo-controlled, clinical trial" in which "Patients were randomly assigned to receive empagliflozin (10 mg once daily) or matching placebo," with allocation performed via "a minimization process with a 10% stochastic element."

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation used a central minimization algorithm with a stochastic element (implying concealed, computer-generated central allocation) with matching placebo and double-blind design, and baseline characteristics across the two groups of ~3300 each were near-identical (age 63.9 vs 63.8, eGFR 37.4 vs 37.3, diabetes 46.2% vs 45.8%), consistent with chance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Patients were randomly assigned to receive empagliflozin (10 mg once daily) or matching placebo. Randomization was performed with the use of a minimization process with a 10% stochastic element."

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and carers were blinded by matching placebo, a run-in phase selected adherent patients, adherence was high and balanced (89.6% vs 90.3% taking >80% of tablets), non-study SGLT2 inhibitor use was minimal (0.5% vs 0.9%), and all analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle including all randomized patients.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "All the analyses were performed according to the intention-to-treat principle and included data from all patients who had undergone randomization, including data collected from the time of the formal interim analysis to the final follow-up visits."

domain_judgments.rationale: Follow-up was essentially complete, with 99.1% of patients completing final follow-up or having died, vital status missing for only 0.3% and consent withdrawn by 0.6% — far too few to bias the effect estimate.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "In total, 6552 patients (99.1%) were alive and completed final follow-up or had died during followup. Vital status was missing for 18 patients (0.3%), and 39 patients (0.6%) withdrew consent."

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary composite outcome relies on objective central-laboratory creatinine/eGFR measurements and hard events (dialysis, transplant, death), applied identically in both groups, and all component events were adjudicated by clinicians blinded to treatment allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "All events of death, potential hospitalizations for heart failure, myocardial infarction, stroke, liver injury, ketoacidosis, lower-limb amputation, acute kidney injury, and serious genital infections were adjudicated by clinicians who were unaware of trial-group assignments"

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered (NCT03594110; EudraCT 2017-002971-24) with a publicly available protocol and statistical analysis plan, the primary and key secondary outcomes and subgroups were prespecified with prespecified multiplicity control (Hochberg, familywise error 0.029) and a protocol-specified single interim analysis; the only minor consideration is early stopping for efficacy at a prespecified boundary, which can modestly overestimate effects but was governed by pre-set stringent criteria.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The prespecified primary outcome was the first occurrence of progression of kidney disease or death from cardiovascular causes... The protocol and the full statistical analysis plan are available at www.empakidney.org."

overall_summary: All five RoB 2 domains were judged at low risk: central minimization-based randomization with balanced baseline characteristics, double-blind placebo control with high balanced adherence and intention-to-treat analysis, 99.1% complete follow-up, objective centrally measured and blindly adjudicated outcomes, and prespecified outcomes/analyses in a registered protocol and published statistical analysis plan. The only residual considerations — industry sponsorship (with independent academic analysis at Oxford) and early stopping at a prespecified efficacy boundary — are not sufficient to raise concerns in any domain.
